## blowhorn upgrade

Carry this Mac's local data from an earlier home into this one. It carries profiles, analytics history, every run-ledger line (duplicates included), the write-back spool, the pause and the settings you changed. The earlier home is left exactly as it was, nothing already in the new home is overwritten, and a file that differs is kept and named in the report. Browser session folders are never carried. The pause is carried first, so a paused Mac is paused in the new home even if a later part fails. Each completed carry is recorded in upgrades.json in the new home, so it runs once; a carry that fails is not recorded and the next run tries again, adding nothing twice. While a scheduled pass is still running from the earlier home the answer is busy and nothing is touched. The earlier home is found from `--source`, then from the engine record the app wrote before this launch, then from the previous checkout at ~/code/blowhorn. A folder that belongs to another macOS user is never carried, even when named with `--source`; the report says so and carries nothing. `--dry-run` -- including one that comes from your settings -- only plans: the answer is planned, nothing is written, and the upgrade is still due. The desktop app runs this itself at launch; you never need a terminal for it.

```text
blowhorn upgrade [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--source` | string |  | The earlier version's home to carry data from; without it the engine record from before this launch is read, then the previous checkout at ~/code/blowhorn |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the report as one JSON object: ok, status (upgraded, planned, current, busy or failed), dry_run, target, source, a one-line summary, and one entry per step with its counts and any files kept |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn upgrade`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn upgrade` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |
| `--risk-profile` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn upgrade` because `--risk-profile` is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn upgrade
blowhorn upgrade --dry-run
blowhorn upgrade --dry-run --json
blowhorn upgrade --source ~/code/blowhorn-old
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.
